RBI Master Direction — Digital Lending (2022) — Key excerpts for CreditShield policy alignment

1. Key Fact Statement (KFS)
Regulated entities must provide a standardised Key Fact Statement before contract execution. The KFS must disclose all-inclusive cost of digital loans (annualised interest, fees, insurance, other charges), cooling-off rights, grievance redressal, and loan servicing terms. Any material change post-sanction requires refreshed consent and updated KFS where applicable.

2. Cooling-off period
Borrowers must be given an explicit cooling-off period (look-off window) during which they may exit the digital loan without penalty, paying only principal and pro-rata interest as specified. The cooling-off mechanism must be disclosed in KFS and accessible in the borrower journey.

3. Direct disbursement mandate
Loan proceeds must be disbursed directly to the borrower’s bank account with the RE (or as permitted under applicable structure). Pass-through of disbursal solely to third-party pools without borrower visibility is not permitted except where regulation explicitly allows documented escrow structures.

4. Loan recovery conduct
Recovery agents must follow fair practices: no harassment, no impersonation, prescribed calling windows, documented authorisation trail, and alignment with RBI fair practices code. Digital lending service providers (LSPs) remain accountable for outsourced recovery behaviour under outsourcing governance.

5. Account Aggregator (AA) framework
Where cash-flow underwriting uses consented bank data, entities should prefer Account Aggregator–mediated flows with clear purpose limitation, FIP–FIU consent artefacts, and data minimisation. AA usage does not replace KYC, fraud controls, or internal credit policy.

6. Data localisation note (operational)
For Indian lending operations, store and process borrower PII and credit data in jurisdictions and cloud regions compliant with RBI circulars on storage, access logging, and breach notification. ap-south-1 (Mumbai) is commonly used for in-region processing when architecting cloud AI workloads.

CreditShield Hard Rejection Rules (HR-01 — HR-07)

HR-01 — FOIR maximum breach
- Condition: Fixed Obligations to Income Ratio exceeds product cap.
- Threshold: FOIR > 65% → auto REJECT.
- RBI / policy reference: Internal credit policy aligned to prudent retail underwriting; FOIR caps mirror board-approved risk appetite.
- Exceptions: None for unsecured retail; secured products may use board-approved lower FOIR if documented (not auto-approved here).
- Example: Declared income ₹50,000; existing EMIs ₹36,000; FOIR 72% → HR-01.

HR-02 — Document tamper / integrity failure
- Condition: Cryptographic or forensic integrity check fails on salary slip, bank statement, or ITR XML/hash mismatch.
- Threshold: Any tamper flag on income-critical docs → REJECT + fraud flag.
- Reference: Digital lending conduct + internal fraud policy.
- Exceptions: Re-upload allowed only after full re-verification workflow.
- Example: PDF incremental save mismatch on salary slip → HR-02.

HR-03 — NPA / write-off history
- Condition: Borrower or guarantor NPA / write-off in last 36 months on bureau or internal watchlist.
- Threshold: Any confirmed event → REJECT.
- Reference: Board credit policy + RBI prudential norms context.
- Exceptions: Fully settled with documented NOC and committee waiver (manual path outside auto engine).
- Example: Write-off ₹45k settled 14 months ago still on bureau narrative → HR-03.

HR-04 — Declared vs verified income variance
- Condition: |declared − verified| / verified > 50%.
- Threshold: Breach → REJECT.
- Reference: Income verification SOP.
- Exceptions: None for auto path.
- Example: Declared ₹80k; AA-verified ₹38k → HR-04.

HR-05 — Loan stacking
- Condition: New loan enquiries / disbursals in rolling 90 days.
- Threshold: ≥3 new loans → REJECT.
- Reference: Internal affordability policy.
- Exceptions: None auto; secured top-up with lien may be manual exception.
- Example: Four new unsecured facilities in 60 days → HR-05.

HR-06 — Bureau score floor
- Condition: CIBIL / Experian bureau score below product floor.
- Threshold: Unsecured personal <550; home loan <600 → REJECT

HR-06 — Bureau score floor
- Condition: CIBIL / Experian bureau score below product floor.
- Threshold: Unsecured personal <550; home loan <600 → REJECT (product-specific tables).
- Reference: Credit bureau usage policy.
- Exceptions: Thin-file programme with guarantor (manual).
- Example: CIBIL 531 personal loan → HR-06.

HR-07 — Income below product minimum
- Condition: Verified monthly income below product threshold.
- Threshold: Per loan_products.txt → REJECT.
- Reference: Product programme rules.
- Exceptions: Co-borrower income aggregation if policy allows (manual verification).
- Example: Verified ₹18k vs personal loan min ₹25k → HR-07.

CreditShield Soft Review Rules (SR-01 — SR-05)

SR-01 — Income coefficient of variation
- Condition: Income CV > 30% on verified inflows (AA / bank analytics).
- Action: MANUAL REVIEW.
- Reference: Variable income playbook.
- Exceptions: Seasonal occupation codes with documented seasonality factor may downgrade severity (analyst decision).
- Example: Freelancer CV 34% → SR-01.

SR-02 — Missing ITR and GST (self-employed)
- Condition: Employment class = self-employed AND no ITR AND no GST where GST registration is expected for stated turnover.
- Action: MANUAL REVIEW.
- Reference: Self-employed income verification SOP.
- Exceptions: Profession codes exempt from GST by statute (documented).
- Example: Consultant, no ITR, no GST → SR-02.

SR-03 — Fraud probability band
- Condition: Model fraud probability between 25% and 50%.
- Action: MANUAL REVIEW.
- Reference: Fraud analytics policy.
- Exceptions: None auto above 50% (escalate to SR-03 high band / HR as applicable).
- Example: Fraud score 32% → SR-03.

SR-04 — Salary gap
- Condition: Gap between salary credits >2 months in lookback window.
- Action: MANUAL REVIEW.
- Reference: Payroll continuity checks.
- Exceptions: Documented leave / maternity with employer letter.
- Example: No salary credit for 3 months → SR-04.

SR-05 — New-to-credit
- Condition: Bureau age <12 months.
- Action: MANUAL REVIEW.
- Reference: Thin-file programme rules.
- Exceptions: Secured gold / LAP with strong collateral may use alternate scorecard (manual).
- Example: First bureau trade 8 months old → SR-05.

CreditShield Loan Programmes — Eligibility snapshot (illustrative; board-approved tables are source of truth)

Personal Loan
- Typical verified income minimum: ₹25,000/month (metro tier may differ).
- FOIR cap: 65% (auto engine).
- Typical CIBIL floor: 550 unsecured.
- Tenure: 12–60 months (programme dependent).

Home Loan
- Typical verified income minimum: ₹35,000/month.
- FOIR cap: 65% (some LTV bands stricter).
- Typical CIBIL floor: 600.
- Tenure: up to 30 years subject to retirement age policy.

MSME / Business
- Typical minimum annual turnover evidence: programme-specific; often GST + 12M banking.
- FOIR / DSCR blended metrics apply; FOIR auto rule may be supplemented by analyst DSCR.
- Tenure: 12–84 months common for working capital term loans.

Vehicle Loan
- Typical verified income minimum: ₹20,000/month.
- FOIR cap: 65% with LTV adjustments.
- Secured bureau floors typically lower than unsecured personal but policy still enforces HR-06 variant by product code.

BNPL
- Typical verified income minimum: ₹15,000/month for revolving BNPL lines.
- Lower ticket sizes; stricter velocity and stacking checks (HR-05 especially).
- Tenure: revolving; pay-in-4 products use shorter windows.

Risk score bands (engine output 0–100)
- 0–35 REJECT
- 36–50 REVIEW
- 51–65 CAUTION
- 66–80 APPROVE
- 81–100 PREMIUM APPROVE

CreditShield IVL grid — Income Verification Layer parameters (7 categories; 48 coded IDs)

Category weights (default retail unsecured personal loan engine):
- IS Income Stability — 28%
- CF Cash Flow Behaviour — 22%
- EP Expense Pattern — 15%
- ST Suspicious Transactions — 18%
- FD Financial Discipline — 10%
- LB Liabilities & Obligations — 4%
- DF Digital Footprint — 3%

Per-parameter score: 0–100 where higher is better unless noted as “inverted” in computation spec.

IS-01..IS-07: pay continuity, employer stability, payroll regularity, bonus predictability, secondary income share, probation status, industry risk overlay.
CF-01..CF-07: inflow cadence, AA vs stated income reconciliation, EMI bounce history, surplus after EMIs, liquidity buffer days, volatile credits %, round-tripping flags.
EP-01..EP-07: essential spend ratio, discretionary spike index, rent-to-income, medical/education stress markers, lifestyle drift, subscription burden, cash withdrawal pattern.
ST-01..ST-07: velocity vs peers, counterpart risk, circular transfers, crypto / gaming adjacency, high-risk MCC concentration, structuring heuristics, dormant account reactivation.
FD-01..FD-07: savings rate trend, insurance discipline, tax filing consistency, emergency fund proxy, delinquency recency, utilisation of revolving credit, limit increase behaviour.
LB-01..LB-06: FOIR components, guarantor load, contingent liabilities, lease obligations, child support / court orders, co-applicant DTI.
DF-01..DF-07: device risk, geo consistency, KYC digital trail age, email/phone tenure, consent log quality, LSP interaction anomalies, account takeover indicators.

Weighting note: Category weight applies to the mean of parameter scores inside the category for the composite IVL score in the mock engine; production may use loan-type-specific matrices from the model governance catalogue.

# Fraud rules (placeholder)

- Velocity checks on new-to-bank applications with thin bureau files default to manual review.
- Device and IP mismatch across login and application submission require step-up verification.
- Synthetic identity indicators (mismatched DOB across documents) block auto-approval.

# Loan / underwriting rules (placeholder)

- FOIR and DTI caps follow product schedule in loan_products and IVL parameter sheets.
- Top-up requests require no DPD beyond grace in the last 12 months on the base facility.
- Co-borrower income may be included only when documented and verified per policy.
